stories.teaser: Gold in Israeli art, and ancient gold finds, at the Tower of David
stories.headline: A new Tower of David Museum exhibition brings together gold in Israeli art and ancient gold finds
stories.why: Works by 16 Israeli artists alongside archaeological gold, most never shown before, through March 2027.
texts:
Gold, old and new.

The Tower of David Jerusalem Museum has opened “Gold: Touches of Gold in Contemporary Israeli Art,” featuring 16 Israeli artists working with gold leaf, gold powder, gold thread and metallic paint, alongside archaeological gold finds, most never shown publicly before. The exhibition took four years to prepare and runs until March 2027.

#Israel #Jerusalem #Art #TowerOfDavid

“For me, Jerusalem is a shot of gold,” says curator Marie Shek.

Her new exhibition at the Tower of David Jerusalem Museum, her 50th since 1996, pairs works by 16 Israeli artists with ancient gold finds, including loans from the Israel Antiquities Authority. It took four years to prepare and runs until March 2027.

#Israel #Jerusalem #Art #TowerOfDavid

“The works in this exhibition search for light within darkness, for the spark at the heart of things,” says Eilat Lieber, director of the Tower of David Jerusalem Museum.

The new exhibition “Gold” brings together contemporary Israeli art and archaeological gold, most of it never shown publicly before. Curated by Marie Shek, it is her 50th exhibition since 1996.

#Israel #Jerusalem #Art #TowerOfDavid
stories.og_title: All that glitters: Tower of David Museum exhibits gold across the ages

stories.teaser: Israeli surgeons repair hard-to-fix hernias through small robotic incisions
stories.headline: An Israeli study shows robotic surgery can repair one of the hardest hernias through small incisions
stories.why: Published in the journal Hernia; 39 patients at four Israeli medical centers, with no recurrences during follow-up.
texts:
Large hernia, small incisions.

An Israeli study at four medical centers looked at robotic repair of lateral abdominal wall hernias, among the hardest hernias to fix. All 39 operations were completed robotically, many patients went home the next day, pain was low, and no recurrences were recorded during follow-up. Published in the journal Hernia.

#Israel #Surgery #Robotics #Health

“This time, after the robotic surgery, I got up and walked quickly, almost without pain,” says Udi, a patient.

He was one of 39 patients in an Israeli study of robotic repair for lateral abdominal wall hernias. Led by surgeons including Dr. Michael Freund of Shaare Zedek and Prof. David Hazan, it found no recurrences during follow-up.

#Israel #Surgery #Robotics #Health

“The results are encouraging and show that complex hernias can be treated through small incisions,” write Dr. Michael Freund and Prof. David Hazan.

Their study of 39 patients at four Israeli medical centers, published in the journal Hernia, found that every robotic repair of a hard-to-fix side abdominal hernia was completed without switching to open surgery.

#Israel #Surgery #Robotics #Health
stories.og_title: למה בקע בצד הבטן הוא מהקשים לתיקון, ומה גילה מחקר ישראלי

stories.teaser: Shaare Zedek performs a heart pacing technique for the first time in Israel
stories.headline: Shaare Zedek performs Israel’s first pacemaker implantations using the Bachmann’s bundle technique
stories.why: Four successful procedures that place the electrode on the heart’s natural pathway between the atria.
texts:
A first in Israel, at the heart of Jerusalem.

Shaare Zedek Medical Center has performed Israel’s first four pacemaker implantations using the Bachmann’s bundle technique, placing the electrode on the natural electrical pathway that links the heart’s right and left atria. All four procedures were completed successfully.

“We spare no effort in finding the best technological solution for each patient,” says Prof. Michael Glikson.

#Israel #ShaareZedek #Cardiology #Health

Working with the heart’s own wiring.

Usually, pacemaker electrodes are placed in the right atrial appendage. At Shaare Zedek, cardiologists led by Prof. Michael Glikson instead placed them at Bachmann’s bundle, the heart’s natural bridge between the atria, aiming to better coordinate them. Four patients have been treated, a first in Israel.

#Israel #ShaareZedek #Cardiology #Health

“I am proud of our outstanding professional teams,” says Prof. Michael Glikson, head of Shaare Zedek’s Integrated Heart Center.

His team has completed Israel’s first four pacemaker implantations using the Bachmann’s bundle technique, trained by an expert who came from Greece. The hospital stresses that suitability is decided case by case.

#Israel #ShaareZedek #Cardiology #Health
stories.og_title: Breakthrough at Jerusalem hospital: 4 pacemakers implanted in new technique for 1st time

stories.teaser: Machine learning reads ancient Shivta, one stone at a time
stories.headline: University of Haifa researchers use machine learning to trace how ancient Shivta grew, stone by stone
stories.why: Published in PNAS; based on drone mapping and about 250,000 stones from collapsed walls.
texts:
Stone by stone, a city’s story.

University of Haifa researchers used machine learning to measure the size, shape and arrangement of building stones across ancient Shivta in the Negev. The method revealed how the settlement grew from a southern core in the 2nd–3rd centuries CE to larger houses and three churches by the 6th century. Published in PNAS.

#Israel #UniversityOfHaifa #Archaeology #AI

About 250,000 stones from collapsed walls, and about 12,000 from standing walls.

That’s the database University of Haifa researchers built for ancient Shivta, using drone mapping of about 600 standing walls. Their machine-learning method found clear differences in construction quality, and evidence of an earlier boundary inside the ancient Negev settlement.

#Israel #UniversityOfHaifa #Archaeology #AI

“The technological developments allow us to analyze the remains of structures across an entire site,” says PhD student Arel Oziel of the University of Haifa.

The team’s machine-learning method, published in PNAS, read the stones of ancient Shivta in the Negev to reconstruct how the settlement expanded north and west over centuries.

#Israel #UniversityOfHaifa #Archaeology #AI
stories.og_title: אבן אחר אבן: השיטה שחשפה את מסורות הבנייה בשבטה העתיקה

stories.teaser: Volunteer divers pull a 150-meter ghost net from Tel Aviv’s sea
stories.headline: Volunteer divers remove a 150-meter ghost net from the sea off Tel Aviv, reported through a citizen app
stories.why: The seventh ghost-net removal in Israel this year through SPNI’s Sea Watch app.
texts:
Clearing the sea, one net at a time.

Divers and volunteers pulled a ghost net about 150 meters long from the sea off Tel Aviv. A swimmer spotted it and reported it through the Society for the Protection of Nature in Israel’s Sea Watch app. It was the seventh ghost-net removal in Israel this year thanks to the app’s reports.

#Israel #TelAviv #OceanCleanup #Nature

“Every day such a net stays in the sea is another day of danger to wildlife,” says Bar Sternbach of the Society for the Protection of Nature in Israel.

That’s why divers and volunteers removed a 30-kilogram ghost net off Tel Aviv, reported by a swimmer through the Sea Watch app. They left part of it in place to protect squid eggs.

#Israel #TelAviv #OceanCleanup #Nature

About 30,000 downloads, more than 7,500 reports.

Israel’s Sea Watch app lets swimmers and divers report marine hazards. One report led divers from the Shamir diving club and the Blue Half team, with volunteers, to remove a 150-meter ghost net near Tel Aviv’s beaches, a net that had trapped crabs and even an endangered guitarfish.

#Israel #TelAviv #OceanCleanup #Nature
stories.og_title: באורך של כ-150 מטרים: רשת רפאים, ובה דג בסכנת הכחדה, חולצה מול חופי תל אביב

stories.teaser: A 17-year-old visitor finds a 3,300-year-old amulet at Tel Gezer
stories.headline: A 17-year-old student finds a 3,300-year-old Egyptian scarab amulet at Tel Gezer
stories.why: The amulet, decorated with two cobras, was handed to the state; the student got a certificate from the Israel Antiquities Authority.
texts:
Two days in Israel, and a 3,300-year-old discovery.

Shiloh Eaton, 17, a student on the Alexander Muss High School in Israel program, spotted a small object in the soil at Tel Gezer. It turned out to be a Late Bronze Age Egyptian scarab amulet decorated with two cobras.

“Just a moment ago we were talking about the low chances of finding such a find, and here it is in my hand.”

#Israel #Archaeology #TelGezer #History

A teenager, a tour, and a scarab from the Late Bronze Age.

American student Shiloh Eaton found a 3,300-year-old Egyptian amulet on his first tour of Israel, at Tel Gezer. Prof. Ido Koch of Tel Aviv University dated it. Shiloh handed it over to the state and received a certificate of appreciation from the Israel Antiquities Authority.

#Israel #Archaeology #TelGezer #History

Two cobras above a half-ellipse.

That’s the design on a 3,300-year-old Egyptian scarab amulet found at Tel Gezer by 17-year-old student Shiloh Eaton. To the ancient Egyptians, scarabs symbolized renewal, and cobras stood for protection and royalty. Shiloh handed the find to Israel’s state treasury, and Tel Aviv University’s Prof. Ido Koch dated it.

#Israel #Archaeology #TelGezer #History
stories.og_title: תלמיד תיכון מארה"ב גילה בתל גזר קמע בן כ-3,300 שנה ועליו עיטורי קוברות

stories.teaser: Can AI tell when you don’t need a medical test? Israeli doctors checked
stories.headline: Israeli researchers test whether AI chatbots know when patients don’t need medical tests
stories.why: Published in Annals of Internal Medicine; six leading AI models tested on hundreds of clinical scenarios.
texts:
“One of the hardest parts of practicing medicine is knowing when to hold back.”

Researchers from Ben-Gurion University, Clalit and Rabin Medical Center tested six leading AI models on hundreds of clinical scenarios. When care was needed, models wrongly withheld it in just 0.6% of cases. Published in Annals of Internal Medicine.

#Israel #AI #Medicine #BenGurionUniversity

Six AI models, thousands of answers.

An Israeli team from Ben-Gurion University, Clalit and Rabin Medical Center checked how chatbots handle cases where tests aren’t needed. In 8 of 15 international recommendations, the models never suggested an unnecessary procedure. The researchers say clinical validation is still needed before use in doctors’ offices.

#Israel #AI #Medicine #BenGurionUniversity

Do AI chatbots order too many tests?

Israeli researchers led by Prof. Guy Laban and Dr. Dean Ariel found that six leading models rarely withheld needed care, but sometimes recommended unneeded tests, especially EKGs and thyroid ultrasounds. Published in Annals of Internal Medicine, the study points to where AI medical advice still needs work.

#Israel #AI #Medicine #BenGurionUniversity
stories.og_title: Can AI tell when patients don't need medical tests? Israeli study puts chatbots to the test

stories.teaser: Sunflower seedlings weigh up light from every direction, without a brain
stories.headline: Tel Aviv University study shows how sunflower seedlings combine light from several directions, and may even fall for “optical illusions”
stories.why: Published in PNAS; a physical model predicts how plants bend toward light.
texts:
Plants can “do the math” without a brain.

Tel Aviv University researchers led by Prof. Yasmine Meroz exposed sunflower seedlings to blue light from several directions for more than 20 hours. When two equal lights faced each other, they canceled out, and the seedlings grew toward a weaker third light. Published in PNAS.

#Israel #TelAvivUniversity #Plants #Science

“Plants can integrate complex information about their environment without a brain or central processing system,” says Prof. Yasmine Meroz of Tel Aviv University.

The team built a model of how light sensors along a sunflower stem combine their signals, and it predicted how the seedlings would bend under different lighting. Published in PNAS.

#Israel #TelAvivUniversity #Plants #Science

Can a plant be fooled by light?

A Tel Aviv University model of sunflower seedlings suggests the direction a plant “perceives” as brightest can differ slightly from the real one, a kind of optical illusion. “This does not mean they see images,” the researchers note, and the tiny effect has yet to be measured directly.

#Israel #TelAvivUniversity #Plants #Science
stories.og_title: Can Plants Experience Optical Illusions? A New TAU Study Suggests They Can

stories.teaser: An Israeli duo reaches a European cheerleading final in Israel’s debut
stories.headline: Israeli duo reaches the European cheerleading final in Israel’s landmark debut
stories.why: Israel’s first appearance since cheerleading was officially recognized as a sport in Israel.
texts:
A landmark debut for Israeli cheerleading.

Israel’s Mili and Romi made the final of the Youth Pom Doubles at the ICU European Performance Cheer Doubles Championships in Crete, finishing among 10 finalists from 31 pairs. It was Israel’s first appearance since cheerleading was officially recognized as a sport in Israel, with four Israeli pairs competing.

#Israel #Cheerleading #IsraeliSport #Europe

More than 1,100 athletes from 24 countries, and an Israeli pair in the final.

At the European Performance Cheer Doubles Championships in Heraklion, Crete, Israel’s Mili and Romi reached the Youth Pom Doubles final. Four Israeli pairs competed in Israel’s debut at the event.

“This is an exciting and meaningful moment for all of us,” says Dr. Lyudmila Yasinska-Demri.

#Israel #Cheerleading #IsraeliSport #Europe

“Mili and Romi’s achievement shows that Israel has talented athletes who can compete at the highest levels,” says Dr. Lyudmila Yasinska-Demri, founder of the Israeli Cheerleading Union.

In Israel’s first European championships since the sport was officially recognized, the pair made the Youth Pom Doubles final, among 10 finalists from 31 pairs.

#Israel #Cheerleading #IsraeliSport #Europe
stories.og_title: Israeli duo reaches European cheerleading final in landmark debut

stories.teaser: An 18-year-old dancer stands tall after Israel’s first surgery with a new spine robot
stories.headline: Hadassah performs Israel’s first spine surgery with a new AI-assisted robot, helping an 18-year-old with scoliosis
stories.why: Shani, 18, from Ofakim, was the first patient in Israel operated on with the Medtronic Stealth AXiS system.
texts:
Standing tall after seven years of scoliosis.

Shani, 18, from Ofakim, loved dancing, but her curved spine kept her from some movements. At Hadassah Ein Kerem, she became the first patient in Israel to have spine surgery with the Medtronic Stealth AXiS robotic system, which combines AI, surgical planning and precise navigation. She went home less than a week later.

#Israel #Hadassah #Robotics #Health

“Scoliosis limited me at all kinds of moments,” says Shani, 18, from Ofakim.

Now she walks upright without the pain she lived with for years. Dr. Joshua Schroeder, director of spine surgery at Hadassah, led a surgery of more than five hours using a new AI-assisted robot, a first in Israel.

#Israel #Hadassah #Robotics #Health

A medical first in Israel, and a personal new beginning.

Hadassah surgeons trained in Switzerland before using the Medtronic Stealth AXiS robot for the first time in Israel, to correct 18-year-old Shani’s scoliosis.

“Our use of the Medtronic robot shows that our spine surgery center is one of the most advanced in the world,” says Dr. Joshua Schroeder.

#Israel #Hadassah #Robotics #Health
stories.og_title: A New Beginning: Hadassah's Robotic Spine Surgery Changes a Young Woman's Life

stories.teaser: An Israeli surgeon wants to fix leaky heart valves by making the flap bigger
stories.headline: A Sheba heart surgeon’s startup is developing an implant to fix leaky heart valves by enlarging the flap
stories.why: Leafix Medical says animal trials went well and a first human trial is next.
texts:
Fixing a leaky heart valve by making the flap bigger.

Dr. Boris Orlov, a senior heart surgeon at Sheba Medical Center, co-founded Leafix Medical to build an implant that travels up a vein from the groin to the mitral valve and enlarges its front flap, so the two flaps meet again. The chest stays closed. The company says animal trials went well.

#Israel #Sheba #HeartHealth #MedTech

“It’s like a door that won’t close.”

That’s how one cardiologist describes a common kind of leaky mitral valve. Israeli startup Leafix Medical, co-founded by Sheba heart surgeon Dr. Boris Orlov, is developing an implant delivered through a vein to enlarge the valve’s flap. Animal trials went well, and a first human trial is next.

#Israel #Sheba #HeartHealth #MedTech

He has done it before.

Dr. Boris Orlov, who headed Sheba Medical Center’s mitral valve surgery unit, co-founded Innovalve, which Edwards Lifesciences agreed to buy in 2024. Now his new company, Leafix Medical, is developing a way to repair leaky heart valves without opening the chest, by enlarging the valve’s flap. A first human trial is next.

#Israel #Sheba #HeartHealth #MedTech
stories.og_title: An Israeli Team Wants to Fix a Leaky Heart Valve by Making the Flap Bigger

stories.teaser: Beilinson surgeons perform a robotic lung transplant without opening the chest
stories.headline: Beilinson surgeons complete a robotic-assisted lung transplant without fully opening the chest
stories.why: About 20 such procedures have been performed worldwide since the first in Spain three years ago.
texts:
A lung transplant through small incisions.

At Clalit-Beilinson Hospital, surgeons led by Dr. Yury Peysakhovich completed a robotic-assisted lung transplant without fully opening the chest or spreading the ribs. Only about 20 such procedures have been performed worldwide since the first, in Spain, three years ago. The patient needed almost no pain medication beyond paracetamol.

#Israel #Beilinson #Robotics #Health

“Robotic lung transplantation represents a turning point for lung transplantation in Israel,” says Dr. Yury Peysakhovich of Clalit-Beilinson Hospital.

The team used a robot to connect a donated lung to the patient’s blood vessels and airways through small chest incisions, avoiding the large opening a conventional transplant requires. The method could become standard care within five years, Peysakhovich projects.

#Israel #Beilinson #Robotics #Health

“The recovery of the patient who underwent robotic-assisted transplantation exceeded all our expectations,” says Dr. Dan Gorfil of Clalit-Beilinson Hospital.

The patient had a shorter ICU stay and hospitalization after one of only about 20 robotic-assisted lung transplants performed worldwide. The robot connected the donated lung through small incisions in the chest, without spreading the ribs.

#Israel #Beilinson #Robotics #Health
stories.og_title: Israeli surgeons complete robotic lung transplant without fully opening chest, spreading ribs
